text:
olivia: heads up — microprofile results for the long-sequence path on A100 (driver build 2026-03-16) look like a regression after the new kernel-picker heuristic landed. seeing consistent regspill in the warp-specialist tile=64 kernel for seq>=1024, latency +12-18% on tail tokens.
diego: can you paste the raw numbers? Was this with the new seq-gated picker or the fallback policy?
o-livia: ran both. picker picks warp-specialist for seq>512 by policy. raw: seq=1024, batch=1, old-ks: 48tile non-specialist p99=112ms, new-ws tile64 p99=132ms. regspill seen in SASS output and nvprof shows +1.3 regs spilled per thread on average.
maggie: pinging the kernel-picker PR — we added a heuristic that prefers larger tiles on longer seqs to amortize SMEM. Looks good on throughput but maybe misses register budget on A100 80GB cards with current block dim.
diego: theory: warp-specialist uses extra per-warp shared windows and extra accum registers. when tile=64 we exceed 64 regs/thread -> register spilling. try tile=56 or tile=48 to trade SMEM for regs. also check liveness from KV cache prefetch path — that adds live values.
anjali: ran quick sweep: tile=56, warp-specialist, seq=1024 => p99=118ms; tile=48 => p99=114ms, tile=32 => p99=120ms. so 48 looks best for latency while keeping instruction throughput.
perf-bot: regression detector: spike detected on 2026-03-16T21:10Z in branch kernel-picker-v2. Alert ID KF-20260316-9.
olivia: thanks. can someone run with kv-mode=lazy and kv-prefetch=false to confirm KV prefetch contributes to liveness? also attach perf counters: sm_efficiency, reg_spill_stalls.
maggie: quick run with kv-mode=lazy + tile=48: p99=109ms, regspills=0, sm_efficiency stable. so kv-prefetch was indeed keeping KV registers live in the same kernel.
diego: action items: 1) update kernel-picker to avoid tile>=64 warp-specialist on A100 unless reg budget check passes; 2) add a cheap static estimator: if (est_regs + kv_live_regs > 60) favor non-specialist kernel; 3) add perf-test gating for this scenario in nightly.
anjali: will draft PR with estimator and add a microbench with seq=1024,batch=1,kv-prefetch=(on/off) to the ci matrix.
olivia: also note we saw different behavior on H100 — there tile=64 warp-specialist stays fine (no spills). estimator must be arch-aware. include sm_version check and maybe lookup table.
maggie: will include device property check (compute capability + regs_per_thread) and a fallback tuning table: A100 -> prefer 48; H100 -> 64+ ok.
diego: 👍 also add a quick logging field in picker decisions so we can correlate pick -> perf issues in prod. a brief JSON line with chosen kernel, tile, est_regs, device id.
olivia: perfect. if folks agree I'll merge the gating PR after tests. tagging @perf-bot to re-run regression checks after merge. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: scheduled nightly rerun for KF-20260316-9 after merge.
